canonical_claim: The format-freeze work for `B176` must review envelope TLV fields and make the streamed `gc/snap` codec preserve streaming, compression, and ordering semantics.

In the meta-descriptor raw-body plan, the absent-meta AND absent-body retry mechanism in putBlob's step (Task 3 step 5) is left as an open implementation choice between a sentinel value and a re-throw-ABORTED-and-retry approach; whichever is picked, putBlob and observeAndAdmitByMeta must stay consistent.

The manifest decode cache assumes the backend token uniquely determines content, but the capability probe does not currently test TOKEN⟹CONTENT; a weak recycled token could serve stale manifests. Additionally, The TOKEN⟹CONTENT contract is load-bearing for the manifest cache but is not verified by Cas::Probe. Additionally, Backend tokens must satisfy `head(k).token == prior get(k).token` only when the bytes are unchanged; this contract makes token-based decoded-shard caching safe.
Plain-object helpers casPutObject and casRemoveObject bypass CasRequestController and can retry beyond the lease-bounded retry discipline used by the ref lane.

suppress_destructive is recomputed independently in fold and runRegularRound, so a future anomaly append between those reads could make fold and deletion decisions diverge. Additionally, Any clamp anomaly sets `suppress_destructive` for the pass, preventing graduation and pending or exact-token deletes until a clamp-free pass. Additionally, A clamped GC pass may hold back a landed reference, but must declare the clamp and suppress graduation and pending deletes until a later clamp-free pass consumes the held reference. Additionally, GC computes `suppress_destructive` once from anomalies, carried holds, and incomplete frontiers, and threads it through merge, ref cleanup, and namespace janitor so destructive decisions cannot diverge.; A GC fold that holds back a landed reference must declare the hold; a silent hold-back is unsafe because it can produce the `31 dangling blobs` counterexample.

B140-dangle was caused by separately durable snapshot edges and `folded_cursor`; embedding the cursor in the snap codec makes trim and snap coverage co-durable. Additionally, `CaB140DangleMerge.tla` proves that trim gating and storing the fold cursor with committed snap edges are jointly necessary and sufficient to prevent trim-before-durable dangles.; Snapshot coverage and GC fold coverage are independent: snapshot `X` lets a writer omit logs through `X`, while the folded cursor proves that those logs no longer need to be read for edge discovery; both are required before log deletion.
B140-dangle is pinned by tests requiring a shared deduplicated blob to survive dropping only one of two live refs.

The S04/S04b under-count bug was fixed by replacing persisted integer in-degree with an idempotent source-edge set, making duplicate removals no-ops. Additionally, Source-edge activation is set union and removal is set difference, so refolding either operation is idempotent.
The resurrect-reupload orphan occurs when GC tracks a retired entry by hash only; settling the old token without re-condemning a replacement token can leave the replacement present forever.
B157 read-your-writes coherence increments `shard_write_seq[key]` before cache eviction and prevents a concurrent stale GET from re-caching an invalidated shard decode.

B115 was caused by `ReadBufferFromFileView` retaining a stale `file_offset_of_buffer_end` after remote `setReadUntilPosition` discarded its inner working buffer, which could produce duplicated and missing granules as wrong query results.

The implemented ref lane trusts a cold LIST as complete and enforces strict increase but not middle-log contiguity, so a missing middle log can be silently skipped; the v9 contiguous-chain design exists only in TLA+ models and plans. Additionally, The LIST-liar regression tests intentionally pin current defective behavior: a hidden middle record produces `under_lie.unchecked == 1` and `under_lie.reachable == 0`, while a hidden tail transaction can make fsck report a clean result over a ref set missing an acknowledged publish; fixing `recoverRefTable` is expected to make these tests fail until their assertions are updated. Additionally, A CAS ref-prefix enumeration can omit durable ref-log objects: Probe A observed two holes at 16:47:38 that were missing from the pre-fold scan while HEAD verified both objects as present. Additionally, If `Gc::fold` reads a record only when its key appears in the round's LIST hint, a durable checkpoint-committed ref log omitted by LIST is treated as absent, leaving the namespace held and making the frontier incomplete so destructive work is suppressed.

Deleting and recreating `cas/refs/<ns>/<shard>` under the old path-keyed cursor creates an ABA hazard: a stale `folded_cursor` can skip journal versions 1 through K in the recreated shard, losing its edges.

Without a valid `gc/state` baseline, trimmed journals make a fresh GC interpret long-committed live blobs as zero-in-degree and mass-delete live data; this is fail-catastrophic rather than fail-closed. Additionally, A rebuild over trimmed journals fails closed with `CORRUPTED_DATA` when no healthy adopted baseline exists, rather than silently under-counting live edges.

The queue implementation needed identity-checked map-entry erasure because a slow waiter could otherwise erase a successor queue by key and create two leaders with conflicts; test counters also had to exclude bootstrap and mount-renewal `casPut` operations.
If GC fences a fresh lease before the adopt GET, the old `claimMount` and `claim` checks can resurrect a fenced incarnation under the same epoch, contradicting the terminal-incarnation rule.

A rejected `ALTER TABLE s19_src MOVE PARTITION 2 TO DISK 'default'` correctly raised `Code:479 UNKNOWN_DISK`, but two `CasRootCas` operations occurred before validation, so the move was not perfectly atomic even though fsck remained clean.

Build::promote must stop silently overwriting a committed ref, republishRef must make destination re-drives idempotent, and Build::abandon must retire build_seq only after precommit removal. Additionally, Promoting over a pre-existing committed ref can leave two live Committed bindings for one ref and later make dropRef remove only the new binding, creating owner↔refs divergence. Additionally, The TLA+ model's RefFreeFor guard permits a ref to own at most one committed manifest, so the C++ promote guard is a model-alignment requirement.; Replacing an existing committed ref requires an explicit `owner_transition` removal before promotion; silent displacement is forbidden because GC derives edges from explicit operations rather than state diffs.
With gc_interval_sec=5, GC can condemn a freshly written blob in the putBlob→promote window and cause ordinary INSERT to fail with ABORTED at promote's blob revalidation.

Build::promote's prior fail-closed revalidation aborted on a condemned tokened leaf even though that leaf had a retained writer source; the existing copy-forward pre-pass intentionally handled only tokenless adoptEvidence leaves.
The tokenless race exists because the pre-pass observes retire-view round R while mutateShard may refresh the view to R′, making condemnations in (R,R′] visible only to the in-closure revalidation.

A `tombstone` meta is terminal: a writer must never CAS `tombstone` to `clean`, because GC may already have committed deletion of the unchanged-token body; the writer instead waits boundedly for the meta to become absent and then fresh-uploads, failing with `ABORTED` on exhaustion.
The deterministic GC-delete-versus-writer race must prove that after GC wins `condemned` to `tombstone`, a writer observes the tombstone and fails with `ABORTED` instead of un-tombstoning it.
A deposed leader can leave a durable stray-Clean meta over a still-`delete_pending` blob when `clearSparedMeta` completes before the leader loses the `gc/state` CAS.
Stray-Clean meta lets a writer reuse the condemned exact token, allowing a later pending `deleteExact` to delete the live reuse and violate `INV_NO_LOSS`.

A pre-existing `RunFileReader::seek` bug can skip an exact full key duplicated across a block boundary because it selects the last block with `min_key <= target`; the independent fix is to select the first block with `max_key >= target`.

Before the variable-length digest port, `CasGc.cpp` condemn-sweep and several `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites used `hexToU128` inside `catch(...) { continue; }`, silently classifying every SHA-256 blob as foreign and causing a permanent leak or false-clean fsck result.; The Phase 2 SHA-256 implementation must port the `CasGc.cpp` condemn sweep and `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites in the same change that widens the digest; otherwise the pool silently leaks every SHA-256 blob.
A predecessor PUT that completes after successor recovery can create a late older-epoch log invisible to the successor and later snapshots; a missed `+1` edge is a data-loss class, not merely a leak.
Unconditional staging-to-blob copy is unsafe because the read path does not rehash bodies, so overwriting a live object can expose a torn or short body as valid data.
A dedup shortcut that adopts an existing blob after HEAD without the condemn check can reference a blob pending GC deletion and violate edge-before-observe, causing data loss.
